data.description:
rebar already defines a structured failure discriminator, and only one of its three interfaces uses
it. Over MCP a failure arrives as prose inside an exception message, so an agent that needs to
distinguish "ticket not found" from "concurrency mismatch" from "a gate refused this" must
pattern-match English that no test pins.

## The vocabulary already exists

`src/rebar/schemas/common.schema.json:105-116` defines `error_envelope`:

- `error` — *"Machine error code, e.g. 'ticket_not_found'."* (required)
- `input` — the raw input that failed to resolve (required)
- `message` — human text (required)
- `exit_code` — *"the process exit code that accompanied this failure (see docs/exit-codes.md)"*

It is aliased as a top-level schema (`schemas/error_envelope.schema.json`) and registered as
`ERROR_ENVELOPE` (`schemas/__init__.py:96`).

## Only the CLI emits it

Emitters: `_engine_support/reads_cli.py:165` (`ticket_not_found`), `:170` (`show_failed`), `:411`
(deps reader), `_engine_support/next_batch.py:537`, `signing.py:786` (`ticket_not_found`).

`grep -rn 'error_envelope' src/rebar/mcp_server.py src/rebar/_mcp*.py` returns **nothing**. The MCP
surface has no structured error identity at all.

## Why it matters

MCP's consumer is an agent, which is the caller least able to parse prose reliably and most likely
to branch on the outcome — retry, pick another ticket, escalate, or stop. `docs/mcp-reference.md`
documents `outputSchema` for success shapes; the failure shape is undocumented and unpinned, so any
rewording of an error message is a silent breaking change for every agent that matched on it.

## Related, already filed — do not duplicate

- `2e16-cd19-2323-4ae2` — the CLI encodes a retryable "passed but unsigned" signing disposition that
  MCP drops. Same defect, one instance.
- `f0ff-028a-f5cb-4b66` — `docs/exit-codes.md` covers 41 of 75 commands. The envelope's `exit_code`
  field depends on that vocabulary being complete, so sequence this after or alongside it.

This ticket is the general case: give MCP the discriminator the CLI already emits.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] MCP tool failures carry the `error_envelope` discriminator — at minimum `error` and `message`,
      with `input` where a target was being resolved
- [ ] The error codes emitted over MCP are drawn from the SAME vocabulary the CLI emits; a code
      cannot exist on one interface only
- [ ] The failure shape is declared in the MCP tool contract so consumers can rely on it, and
      `docs/mcp-reference.md` documents it alongside the success `outputSchema`s
- [ ] A test pins each emitted code, so rewording a human message cannot change the machine identity
- [ ] The three interfaces (library, CLI, MCP) agree on the code for the same failure — verified by a
      cross-interface test, not by inspection
- [ ] Existing CLI envelope output is unchanged (no regression for current consumers)
data.title: Give MCP failures the structured error identity the CLI already emits
